newsitem.title: Austria: FOCUS-Austria against strict EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Austria against strict EMU stability pact.

text.p: Austria on Thursday voiced strong opposition to introducing automatic sanctions against members of Europe's planned single currency that failed to enforce strict fiscal stability.

"Austria is against automatic sanctions in the case of non-compliance with the Maastricht stability criteria," Chancellor Franz Vranitzky told a news conference ahead of Friday's European Union summit in Dublin.

His remarks appeared to put Austria, in monetary affairs usually a close ally of Germany, on a collision course with its neighbour, which has called for automatic penalties for countries which violate the criteria after they join the union.
The 1992 Maastricht Treaty set thresholds for membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) in terms of public debt, deficits, inflation, exchange and interest rates.
"Sanctions should be decided on a political basis and not automatically," Vranitzky said.
The chancellor added he thought it unlikely the Dublin Summit would reach a final decision on the stability pact.
"According to our latest information, one should be careful with such expectations," he said.

Both Germany and France, which has supported the idea that penalties should be based on a political decision, on Thursday said they expected European Union members to reach an accord on the proposed stability pact in Dublin.
